messages:
From: Tara Nguyen <tara@pinecone.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Silva <marco@weaviate.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Embeddings ops interop: quick intro + pilot sketch

Hi Rishi,

Quick intro — I'm Tara (partnerships, Pinecone). Marco from Weaviate looped me in after the index-federation conversation last quarter. We think there's a nice opportunity to run a small, focused POC to validate:

- fallback routing from Pinecone to Weaviate for cold tiering;
- S3-backed blob reference passthrough for large documents;
- read/refresh patterns for Redwood's caching layer so KV cache warmups are robust.

Sketch attached: partner-poc-outline.pdf (2 pages) — includes proposed dataset size (~10k docs), perf targets (p95 < 120ms for hot reads, background fallthrough < 2s), and success criteria.

Questions for your team before we schedule a technical sync:
1) Is there a preferred auth pattern for per-tenant keys in Redwood Private deploys?
2) Do you want a single-call routing proof (Redwood -> Pinecone -> Weaviate fallback) or separate integration stubs?

Happy to join a 30–45min tech call next week. Proposed slots in the doc.

Thanks,
Tara Nguyen
Partnerships – Pinecone
Attachment: partner-poc-outline.pdf (pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Nguyen <tara@pinecone.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings ops interop: quick intro + pilot sketch

Thanks Tara 94 this looks promising.

Short answers up front:
- Auth: we prefer short-lived per-tenant service tokens issued by our private control plane; for hosted pilots we can accept static API keys scoped to a test namespace.
- Proof approach: let's do a single-call routing proof so we can measure end-to-end latency impact and KV-cache effectiveness.

I'll add Ben (storage partnerships) and Vanessa (solutions) to scope the work and confirm timelines. High-level Redwood needs for the POC:
- deterministic fallback behavior when Pinecone cold misses (explicit call path + observability hooks),
- an S3 object reference pattern where embeddings point to a blob id but Redwood can fetch metadata without rehydrating full content,
- a recorded eval harness (small prompt set) to measure answer quality differences when vector store fallthrough occurs.

Can your engineering lead join Fri 6/26 10:00-10:45 PT? We can share a minimal runbook and an initial infra checklist (we'll attach our interop checklist prior to the call).

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Partner Integrations – Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0182

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Embeddings ops interop: quick intro + pilot sketch

Forwarding Tara's note with a couple of quick tech flags below.

Ben's notes:
- Quantization/serialization: if Pinecone or Weaviate plan to serve quantized vectors, we need to ensure Redwood's scorer is compatible (float16 vs int8 path). Please list supported serialization formats before the sync.
- Thundering herd during backfills: include a backoff strategy for on-demand rehydration from S3; we should define an explicit retry/queue pattern rather than naive synchronous fallbacks.
- Telemetry: request id propagation and per-token cost attribution need to be present in the POC so we can run cost projections.

I can prep a small infra diagram and a test harness branch (GH-PR-embed-adapter-232) by Thursday. Vanessa, will you take ownership of customer-facing docs / success criteria?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Principal Partnerships Engineer – Redwood Inference
Attachment: (none)

From: Tara Nguyen <tara@pinecone.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Embeddings ops interop: quick intro + pilot sketch

Great 94 thanks for the quick feedback everyone.

We can commit an engineering pair: myself (coord) + Jose (engineer) from Pinecone, and Marco will bring Weaviate's integration lead. Jose will verify vector serialization compatibility (we support float32/float16 and a compact int8 flow in our internal paths).

We've accepted the single-call routing approach. Confirmed items we will bring to the tech sync:
- small dataset (10k docs) pre-seeded to Pinecone;
- an S3 bucket with object references (read-only credentials);
- a short eval set and sample prompts to exercise fallthrough;
- a shared runbook + pre-call checklist (attached).

Please find the pre-call checklist attached: interop-tech-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet). I've created a calendar invite for Fri, 26 Jun 2026 10:00-10:45 PT: https://calendar.redwood.com/meet/rdw-poc-9492

If anything changes ping me and we'll reprioritize slots. Looking forward to the sync.

Best,
Tara Nguyen
